title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #1140: Primes of the Form n - 2x²**

Are there infinitely many n where n - 2x² is prime for all valid x?

**Status: DISPROVED** (Epure-Gica, 2010)

Only 8 values work: {2, 5, 7, 13, 31, 61, 181, 199}.
mathContext: The constraint that n - 2x² be prime for ALL x with 2x² < n is extremely restrictive. As n grows, there are more values of x to check, making it increasingly unlikely all shifts are prime.

title: AllShiftsArePrime
content:
**AllShiftsArePrime n:** For every x with 2x² < n, the value n - 2x² is prime.

For example, AllShiftsArePrime 13 means 13, 11, and 5 must all be prime (they are).

title: n = 2 Verified
content: **Computationally verified:** Only x = 0 applies, and 2 is prime.

title: n = 13 Verified
content:
**Computationally verified:** x ∈ {0, 1, 2} giving 13, 11, 5 — all prime.

Lean's `interval_cases` tactic enumerates all valid x values and `decide` checks primality.

title: n = 4 Fails
content:
**Verified counterexample:** 4 - 2·0² = 4, which is not prime.

This shows that not all n satisfy the property.

title: Epure-Gica: n ≡ 1 (mod 4)
content:
**epure_gica_mod_1:** When n ≡ 1 (mod 4), the only values with AllShiftsArePrime are {5, 13, 61, 181}.

This is Theorem 4.1 from Epure and Gica (2010).

title: Epure-Gica: n ≡ 3 (mod 4)
content:
**epure_gica_mod_3:** When n ≡ 3 (mod 4), only {7, 31, 199} work, with at most one exception.

Uses results of Mollin-Williams (1989) on class numbers of quadratic fields.

title: Even Case
content:
**Verified proof:** Even n > 2 always fail because n - 2·0² = n is even and greater than 2, hence not prime.

This eliminates half of all natural numbers immediately.

title: Erdős Problem #1140: DISPROVED
content:
**erdos_1140:** There do NOT exist infinitely many n with AllShiftsArePrime.

The proof uses the finiteness axiom: there exists a bound B above which no n satisfies the property. Given any proposed infinite sequence, we find n > B, contradicting finiteness.
